references.text: Habakkuk writes that "the righteous shall live by his faith" ([ref:Hab 2:4|Habakkuk 2:4]). John 3:36 expresses the same principle: whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.

[ref:Joh 3:16-18|John 3:16-18] is the immediate context where Jesus himself explains that whoever believes in the only begotten Son shall not perish but have eternal life, while whoever does not believe is already condemned.

[ref:Joh 1:12|John 1:12] says that to all who received him, he gave the right to become children of God—to those who believe in his name. Faith in the Son as the basis for salvation is a recurring theme in John's writings.

Jesus says in [ref:Joh 5:24|John 5:24] that whoever hears his word and believes in him who sent him has eternal life and will not come into judgment. This repeats the promise of eternal life to those who believe.
In [ref:Joh 6:47|John 6:47], Jesus says: "Whoever believes has eternal life." This is a direct parallel to the first part of John 3:36.
[ref:Joh 6:40|John 6:40] emphasizes that it is the Father's will that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him shall have eternal life, and that Jesus will raise them up on the last day.
[ref:1 Joh 5:11-12|1 John 5:11-12] confirms that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.

[ref:Rom 1:17-18|Romans 1:17-18] links righteousness by faith with God's wrath against ungodliness, just as John 3:36 contrasts belief and disobedience toward the Son with eternal life and God's wrath respectively.
[ref:Ef 5:6|Ephesians 5:6] warns that God's wrath comes upon the children of disobedience. This expands on the consequence described in John 3:36 for those who are disobedient to the Son.
[ref:Rom 2:8|Romans 2:8] says that over those who are disobedient to the truth, wrath and anger come. The parallel to God's wrath that "comes upon" the disobedient in John 3:36 is clear.

[ref:1 Joh 5:10|1 John 5:10] says that whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because they have not believed the testimony God gave about his Son. Unbelief toward the Son is thus unbelief toward God himself.

[ref:5 Mos 18:19|Deuteronomy 18:19] warns that whoever does not listen to the words of the prophet whom God sends, God will require an account from them. This points forward to disobedience toward the Son and its consequences.
[ref:Joh 3:14-15|John 3:14-15] speaks of how the Son of Man must be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life. This provides the foundation for the promise in verse 36.

[ref:Hebr 3:18-19|Hebrews 3:18-19] shows that the Israelites could not enter God's rest because of unbelief and disobedience, serving as a warning parallel to the judgment on those who are disobedient to the Son in John 3:36.
